title: ANBERNIC’s Switch Lite clone launches today for under $150
summary: Don't expect to actually play many Switch games on this handheld, though.
body: Credit: Hadlee Simons / Android Authority TL;DR ANBERNIC launches the RG 55G1 today, and it recently revealed pricing for the Android handheld. The device has a recommended starting price of $149.99, but an early bird price of $139.99. Expect a design that’s very similar to the Nintendo Switch Lite, along with a Snapdragon G1 Gen 2 chip, and a 6,000mAh battery. ANBERNIC has been teasing the RG 55G1 for a while now, and it bears more than a passing resemblance to the Nintendo Switch Lite. We’ve already seen the spec sheet, but we’ve finally got pricing. The RG 55G1 launches today, and ANBERNIC has revealed a recommended price of $149.99 for the 4GB/64GB model and $174.99 for the 8GB/128GB variant. However, the company is also offering a $10 discount on each model for the first three days. That means you’re paying $139.99 and $164.99 , respectively.

title: Lake Ontario is now ‘Lake America’ on Google Maps, but not for everyone
summary: US citizen will see the "new" name, while Canadians still see "Lake Ontario."
body: Credit: Andy Walker / Android Authority TL;DR Google Maps is now starting to call Lake Ontario “Lake America” following recent executive orders. Last week, President Trump signed the executive order to rename the lake officially. Google says the new change is only visible for people in the US, while those in Canada will continue to see “Lake Ontario.” Last week, US President Donald Trump signed executive orders to officially rename Lake Ontario “Lake America,” his second re-christening, so to speak, of a body of water after the Gulf of Mexico . Following these official orders, Google Maps has started showing the name of the body of water bordering both the US and Canada. In an official announcement , Google noted it will start showing the lake’s new official name, as designated by the US Geographic Names Information System (GNIS). It said the official name change will appear on Google Maps, but only for people in the US.

title: Gaga Music, Warp Publishing Strike New Partnership
summary: Both independent music businesses have worked together since 2017.
body: MELBOURNE, Australia — Gaga Music , the independent Australian publishing and sync specialist, forms a new partnership with London-based Warp Publishing. Both independent music businesses have worked together since 2017, with Gaga Music initially representing Warp Publishing’s catalogue across Australia and New Zealand, followed by Warp repping Gaga’s catalogue in the United Kingdom. Announced Monday, Aug. 31 on the eve of the 2026 BIGSOUND conference in Brisbane, the new arrangement extends that alliance, with Warp now an active partner in Gaga Music alongside the Australian business’ founder Grant Gillies . At the same time, Warp Publishing director Theo Seffusatti and general manager Nadine Riezouw join Gillies on the board of Gaga as directors. The new deal should “expand global opportunities” for songwriters, composers and represented catalogues, reads a statement. Financial terms weren’t disclosed. “In a climate increasingly shaped by consolidation and external investment, it’s important that independent music companies continue to offer a genuinely creative and ethical alternative in rights management,” comments Gillies. “Warp is an iconic name in the global mus…

title: Dolly Parton’s Legacy on the Billboard 200 Chart: 7 Decades of Hit Albums
summary: She scored more top 40-charted sets in the 2020s than in any other decade.
body: For seven straight decades, from the 1960s on through the 2020s, the late Dolly Parton charted an iconic string of 50 albums on the all-genre Billboard 200 chart during her lifetime — including 15 top 40-charted sets. Following her passing on Aug. 25, Parton racked up a 16th top 40 set with Ultimate Dolly Parton . From her debut with Porter Wagoner on Just the Two of Us in 1969, on through her most recent studio album to debut, 2023’s Rockstar , the singer-songwriter left a remarkable impression on Billboard ’s signature album chart. title: Here Are All the K-pop Albums That Have Topped the Billboard 200: Full List
summary: BTS was the first K-pop act to top the all-genre chart; BLACKPINK was the first female K-pop act to do so.
body: ENHYPHEN ’s THE SIN: BLISS puts K-pop back in a familiar spot — No. 1 on the all-genre Billboard 200 chart. The EP is the 26th album or EP by a K-pop act to reach No. 1 on Billboard’s flagship albums chart in just over eight years. The first was BTS ’ Love Yourself: Tear in June 2018. Stray Kids has amassed nine No. 1 titles on the Billboard 200, which puts them out front among K-pop acts. BTS is second, with seven No. 1 titles. ATEEZ is next in line with three No. 1s. SuperM , BLACKPINK , TOMORROW X TOGETHER , NewJeans , TWICE and ENHYPHEN have all notched one No. 1 to date. In addition, one multi-artist K-pop soundtrack, KPop Demon Hunters , has reached No. 1. title: ENHYPEN Scores First No. 1 Album on Billboard 200 With ‘THE SIN : BLISS’
summary: Plus, Dolly Parton soars into the top five after her passing.
body: ENHYPEN claims its first No. 1 album on the Billboard 200 chart as THE SIN : BLISS debuts atop the ranking (dated Sept. 5). The set earned 98,000 equivalent album units in the United States in its first week (ending Aug. 27), according to Luminate. THE SIN : BLISS marks ENHYPEN’s seventh top 10, all achieved since 2022. The act had previously gone as high as No. 2, twice, with THE SIN : VANISH in January and ROMANCE : UNTOLD in 2024.   Related ENHYPEN Drops Latest Installment in ‘THE SIN’ Series With ‘BLISS’: Stream It Now Here Are All the K-pop Albums That Have Topped the Billboard 200: Full List Forever No. 1: Dolly Parton, ‘9 to 5’ Also in the top 10, Dolly Parton , who died on Aug. 25, tallies her fourth top 10-charted album, as the greatest hits collection Ultimate Dolly Parton reenters the chart at No. 5. The Billboard 200 chart ranks the most popular albums of the week in the U.S. based on multi-metric consumption as measured in equivalent album units, compiled by Luminate. title: Just get a Pixel 11? Here are the first 10 settings you need to change
summary: Set up your new Pixel 11 properly with these 10 essential tweaks.
body: The Google Pixel 11 series is officially out in the wild. As with pretty much every Pixel Google has released before, the new phones aren’t necessarily set up to give you the best experience out of the box. There are plenty of useful features and settings that are either disabled by default or require manual configuration. And with the Pixel 11 series bringing a heap of new software features, there are even more things worth tweaking this year.

title: 5 Android phones you should buy instead of the Google Pixel 11 Pro Fold
summary: These five phones are the Pixel 11 Pro Fold's fiercest competitors.
body: Google is playing catch-up with the new Pixel 11 Pro Fold . The North American foldable market is as competitive as ever, with Samsung, Motorola, and Google all vying for a piece of the pie. Last year’s Google Pixel 10 Pro Fold was largely overshadowed by thinner, lighter foldables, but the Pixel 11 Pro Fold will prove more competitive. This year’s Pixel foldable is thinner, lighter, and more refined than its predecessor. Regardless, there are still a handful of compromises that might push foldable buyers to choose a different Android phone instead.

title: Google made Android 17’s best feature a Pixel 11-exclusive. This free app does it better
summary: Stroll lets me earn time on social media by walking first.
body: Credit: Tushar Mehta / Android Authority Google’s latest Pixel 11 series has been making waves since its announcement earlier this month. If you weren’t so savvy about the (stealthy) upgrades — or the new colors — that it brings, you’d probably pass the phones off as the old Pixel 10 series. But if you do make the effort to inquire about the improvements the Pixel 11 brings, you’ll find a few good, handy additions. A few of these include better control over the camera’s tones , the new, enticing Tap-to-Share , real-time translations for podcasts and videos, and more. One of my favorite inclusions is Android 17’s new Digital Wellbeing feature, called Pause Point . When enabled, it forces you to deliberate whether you truly want to open a possibly distracting app. While it was announced as a core Android 17 feature, Google screwed up big time by limiting it to the Pixel 11 series .

title: There’s no GrapheneOS for Pixel 11 phones because Google cut a key security feature
summary: The GrapheneOS team suggests Google may have dropped this key security feature to 'save money'
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR The team behind GrapheneOS has confirmed that they were unable to complete GrapheneOS for Google Pixel phones. GrapheneOS developers said this was due to Google’s new phones lacking support for the MTE security feature. The team says they might have to skip the Pixel 11 phones as a result and shift focus entirely to Motorola devices. GrapheneOS is the best custom ROM if you want a secure, private experience. Unfortunately, Google recently made it harder for developers to build custom ROMs for Pixel phones. Now, it turns out that the Pixel 11 phones might not get GrapheneOS at all due to a missing security feature. title: The Pixel 11 Pro’s HiLight feature looks cool, but it’s missing 5 big features
summary: The glow-up isn't finished yet.
body: I miss the days when notification LEDs were a thing. I still remember the red light flashing on my BlackBerry whenever a notification came in. I’d immediately pick up my phone and check what I’d missed. Smartphones have mostly left that idea behind. Yes, Nothing did bring it back in its own way with the Glyph lights, but personally, that feels like a little too much of a light show. That’s why Google’s HiLight feature on the Pixel 11 Pro series immediately caught my attention. It feels like a much more modern take on the notification LED I used to love. The light sits neatly inside the camera visor; it can glow in different colors, and it’s quite subtle. But the problem is, after using HiLight, I can’t stop thinking about how much more useful it could be .

title: I need to stop using the Galaxy Z Fold 8, but I can’t
summary: It really is a hard phone to put down.
body: It’s been nearly two weeks since I first put my SIM in the Galaxy Z Fold 8 . I got some hands-on time with the device before picking one up, so I largely knew what to expect. However, what I didn’t anticipate was not wanting to use any other phone afterward. I test over 40 smartphones a year, and I desperately need to move on to other devices, but I’m just having too much fun with the Galaxy Z Fold 8. If you’re using the Galaxy Z Fold 8, you know the feeling extends beyond the initial honeymoon phase. The phone has flaws, and I can easily point them out. However, the mark of an excellent phone is that I look beyond them.

title: Google Messages just got a customization setting I’ve wanted for years — how to use it
summary: It's about time, Google.
body: Google Messages is a solid all-around texting app, but it still lacks some pretty basic features, or has only recently added them. One such feature is custom chat themes. In the year 2026, Google Messages is just now rolling out proper theme customization . As someone who loves tweaking and customizing my Android phone as much as possible, the fact that Google Messages hasn’t supported chat themes until now has been an insane omission. But thankfully, as of late August 2026, chat themes have finally arrived.

title: Vloggers will love this phone and rear screen add-on, but will anyone else?
summary: The OPPO Reno 16 Pro is a solid Android phone with a quirky accessory, but the price tag is a stretch to get it all.
body: I haven’t used an OPPO Reno phone since 2022’s Reno 8 Pro, so I wasn’t really sure what to expect from the Reno 16 Pro () before it arrived. Then I saw that the phone is compatible with an official magnetic case and rear display combo. Evidently, OPPO is jumping on a minor trend we’ve seen in the last year or so, with Xiaomi reviving the integrated rear display while accessory makers have released add-ons that attach via a magnetic connection.

title: Google rounds the week out with Android 17 QPR2 Beta 4 for Pixel testers
summary: Two weeks after the last release, just like clockwork!
body: TL;DR Android 17 QPR2 Beta 4 is now available for Pixel testers to install. The new builds arrive two weeks after Google released QPR2 Beta 3. Like past QPR2 releases, the Pixel 6 and Pixel 6 Pro are no longer supported. With August nearly behind us, Google’s September Feature Drop could be nearly ready to arrive any day now. That’s the software the company’s been testing as Android 17 QPR1, which hit its Beta 9 release earlier this month. But that’s not all that Google’s been cooking up, and we’ve also been following work on what’s likely to be our big year-end update, in development now as QPR2. It’s been two weeks since QPR2 Beta 3 landed, and today Android 17 QPR2 Beta 4 is arriving right on schedule. Google shares that Android 17 QPR2 Beta 4 is arriving today for Pixel testers, either as build CP41.260814.003.A2, or CP41.260814.003.B1, depending on your hardware.

title: Spotify could soon let you host a Jam without Premium
summary: With strings attached, of course.
body: TL;DR Spotify could soon let Free users host their own collaborative Jams, removing the current Premium-only requirement. Jams hosted by Free users may force shuffle, limit skips, and cap the queue for everyone, including Premium participants. App strings in Spotify 9.1.82.19 hint at the change, but there’s no guarantee the feature will actually roll out. Spotify released Jam, a fully collaborative real-time playlist that can be joined by up to 32 individuals, back in September of 2023. It’s one of Spotify’s best features , and it’s turning three next month. To celebrate the occasion, the music streaming giant might finally be ready to make hosting Jams a lot more accessible. For reference, joining and participating in Jams is available to all, but hosting one requires you to be a Spotify Premium subscriber. Essentially, joining someone’s party is a free affair, but if you want to host a party, you’ll have to open up your wallet. That caveat, however, could soon disappear.

title: Now Brief can now tell you what movies you should watch next
summary: One UI 9 Beta 7 brings Netflix recommendations to Now Brief.
body: Credit: Paul Jones / Android Authority TL;DR One UI 9 Beta 7 for the Galaxy S26 lets you add Netflix recommendations to Now Brief. Once enabled, Now Brief will show a “Top picks for you” card. The feature is also available on the Galaxy Z Fold 8, Z Fold 8 Ultra, and Z Flip 8. Samsung just recently started rolling out One UI 9 Beta 7 for the Galaxy S26 series. This update includes a few new additions we’re still discovering, such as new Bixby features . Adding to that list, Now Brief is getting a useful upgrade for movie lovers. Spotted by @Smasithick on X , there’s a new option you can select for Now Brief content. One UI 9 Beta 7 adds a toggle for Netflix. By going to Galaxy AI > Now Brief > Contents, you’ll be able to enable the option. Once enabled, it should appear among Now Brief’s content sources.

title: Haven’t ordered your Pixel 11 yet? Here’s what your trade-in delay is costing you
summary: You should've ordered yesterday!
body: TL;DR Google Store trade-in values toward the Pixel 11 series have dropped. New trade value offered for recent Pixel models is up to $150 lower, but most differences are closer to $50. The new values are in effect through September. Google offered launch-window bonuses for trade-ins toward its new Pixel 11 series, with trades fetching as much as $1,000 (if you were trading a Pixel 10 Pro Fold, anyway). Those bonuses have unfortunately come to an end, and Google’s rolled out new, lower trade-in values. As noted by Droid Life , the Google Store is showing new trade values toward the Pixel 11, 11 Pro, 11 Pro XL, and 11 Pro Fold today. The new amounts are up to $150 lower than yesterday, which isn’t great for anybody who missed the outgoing deals. But most of the new values aren’t quite so drastically different.

title: Galaxy Watch 8 owners in the US can now take One UI 9 Watch for a spin
summary: The beta adds a bunch of visual and functional upgrades to the Watch 8 and Watch 8 Classic.
body: TL;DR Samsung has started rolling out the One UI 9 Watch beta for the Galaxy Watch 8 and Watch 8 Classic in the US. One UI 9 Watch introduces improvements to Samsung Health, visual enhancements, and workout-related upgrades. The US expansion comes after Samsung kicked off the beta for the Galaxy Watch 8 and Watch 8 Classic in South Korea earlier this week. The Galaxy Watch 9 and Ultra 2 come preloaded with Wear OS 7-based One UI 9 Watch. Samsung already started rolling out the beta for its older devices, beginning with the Galaxy Watch 8 and Watch 8 Classic in South Korea earlier this week . Now the company is bringing the beta to users stateside. A Reddit post by a Galaxy Watch 8 owner confirms the expansion of the One UI 9 Watch beta program to the US. We also have access to the full changelog in English here, detailing every new feature introduced with the software. Much like the company’s other betas, users should be able to access it via the banner in the Samsung Members app.

title: Philips Hue shares how Nanoleaf panel control through its app is going to work
summary: Nanoleaf integration is coming to the Philips Hue app, but there are some limits.
body: Credit: Philips Hue TL;DR Philips Hue has posted a support page for Nanoleaf integration. The page states that Nanoleaf panels will behave similarly to a gradient striplight. Controlling the lights through the Hue app will come with a couple of limitations. Earlier this week, leaked images revealed an exciting possibility for many smart light setups. Through that leak, we learned that Nanoleaf panels could soon work with the Philips Hue app through an unannounced wall light module. Now Philips Hue has provided more details on this integration. There’s a new support page on Philips Hue’s website that’s dedicated to Nanoleaf integration. On the support page, the company confirms that its wall light module exists and that you can use it to control your Nanoleaf wall panels through the Hue app. It will work with Nanoleaf Hexagons, Triangles, and Mini Triangles.

title: Apple TV follows Apple Music with a price hike of its own
summary: Now 50% higher than last summer!
body: TL;DR Apple TV prices are going up, with the monthly rate climbing from $12.99 to $14.99. Annual plans and Apple One bundles are similarly getting increases of their own. Apple’s last big price increase was this time last August. Can you imagine living in a world where you woke up one day and discovered that one of your favorite streaming services was lowering its prices? A little “thank you” to all those loyal subscribers? Executives tightening belts in order to make their service more attractive to customers? Alas, that is not the reality we live in, and it feels like these companies will not rest until they’ve taken every last cent from us . Right now, another is doing its duty to help speed that process along. A little over a month ago, Apple Music announced a price increase , albeit a modest one, with the base rate going up just $1 a month. If you saw that as just an opening move, congratulations on your prescience, as now Apple TV is following suit with its own higher prices.

title: Samsung made Privacy Display cool, and another Android brand is almost ready with its own take
summary: Elements of Xiaomi’s upcoming Smart privacy display have just leaked.
body: TL;DR New leak offers a good first look at Xiaomi’s Smart privacy display, the company’s take on Samsung’s hardware feature with a similar name. When available, users will be able to hide their screen from shoulder surfers while viewing specific apps, notifications, or other sensitive pages. The feature is expected to roll out as part of the HyperOS 4 update later this year. Samsung changed the game with the introduction of Privacy Display on the Galaxy S26 Ultra . This tech effectively blacks out the screen when viewed from certain angles, specifically to avoid onlookers’ gaze. Since May, we’ve known that Chinese smartphone brand Xiaomi is working on a similar feature for its own devices. A new leak now gives us a good look at the company’s implementation. In a post on X , leaker Kacper Skrzypek has revealed multiple elements of Xiaomi’s Smart privacy display, which appears fairly similar to Samsung’s iteration. However, since it is expected to be available as part of the Hyper OS 4 update this year, it is likely a software-based solution, unlike Samsung’s version .

title: Roborock’s new robot vacuum is so hands-off, you might forget it’s there
summary: Sit back, relax and let the Qrevo 2 Pro worry about the messy stuff.
body: TL;DR Roborock’s new Qrevo 2 Pro packs 25,000Pa suction and a Dual Anti-Tangle System designed to keep hair from wrapping around its brushes. It can automatically remove its mop pads before cleaning carpets, while Carpet Boost+ and Deep Carpet Cleaning help tackle dirt buried deeper in rugs and carpets. The self-cleaning dock washes, dries, refills, and empties the robot automatically, with up to 65 days between dustbin emptying. The Qrevo 2 Pro launches at a promotional price of $ 550. Robot vacuums are great at saving you from actually vacuuming, but that doesn’t always mean they’re completely hands-off. Hair still gets tangled around the brushes, mop pads need cleaning, and if your home has a mix of hard floors and carpets, there’s always the possibility of a damp mop ending up somewhere it really shouldn’t. Roborock’s new Qrevo 2 Pro wants to make those annoyances much less common, and some of its upgrades sound genuinely useful. That starts with the actual cleaning. The Qrevo 2 Pro comes with 25,000Pa of suction, so it should have more than enough power to deal with the usual mess around the house. Crumbs scattered under the dining table, dust hiding beneath the sofa, pet hai…

title: Galaxy S26’s latest beta update makes Bixby much easier to use
summary: One UI 9 Beta 7 for the S26 adds hands-free Gesture wake-up and home screen widgets.
body: Credit: Tushar Mehta / Android Authority TL;DR With the latest One UI 9 Beta 7 for the Galaxy S26, Samsung has added Gesture wake-up and home screen widgets, making Bixby easier to activate and use. Gesture wake-up allows users to trigger Bixby by holding the phone near their mouth and speaking into the mic. New Bixby widgets include 2×1, 2×2, and 4×2 options that make it easier to input voice or text. Samsung just released One UI 9 Beta 7 for the Galaxy S26 series earlier in the day. The official changelog was light on details, but we’ve found that the update comes with new features such as My FanCam, Call Brief, Custom Cards in Now Brief, and a split Finder-Google Search search bar. Digging deeper, we’ve found that this release also comes with new Bixby features for the Galaxy S26 series, namely widgets and Gesture wake-up. Gesture wake-up for Bixby was released alongside the Galaxy Z8 foldables, and it has now made its way to the Galaxy S26 series in this beta release. When enabled, this feature lets you start talking to Bixby by holding your phone close to your mouth and speaking directly into the mic.

title: Activating VoLTE and Wi-Fi calling on your Pixel just got much easier
summary: Your settings persist after device reboots too.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR Pixel owners can more easily enable VoLTE and Wi-Fi calling, thanks to developer TakaiSaisei’s tweaked Pixel IMS app. The original method of enabling VoLTE and Wi-Fi calling required the original Pixel IMS app and the Shizuku system app. This new approach ditches the Shizuku requirement and also persists across device reboots. One of the biggest problems with using a Pixel phone in an unsupported market is that Google generally doesn’t offer VoLTE or Wi-Fi calling in these countries. Pixel owners have resorted to using workarounds, but a new solution makes life even easier. Korean developer kyujin-cho released the Pixel IMS app back in 2023, which lets you enable VoLTE and Wi-Fi calling on your Pixel in an unsupported market. However, this approach is somewhat complex for newbies, as it also requires you to install and use the Shizuku system tool. Furthermore, this solution requires you to repeat the process after restarting your phone.

title: Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra owners should sit down before they watch JerryRigEverything’s durability test
summary: The Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra gets put through its paces, and there’s one key difference from the Galaxy Z Fold 7.
body: TL;DR The Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra has been put through its paces by JerryRigEverything in a durability test. While the foldable performs as expected in the scratch test, the inner display appears to give up after a bend test. The Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra continues to exhibit decent dust resistance, similar to the Galaxy Z Fold 7. The Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra is finally here, though some variants are facing delayed shipments due to high demand . It’s not uncommon for a newly released flagship phone to be put through its paces in durability tests, and Samsung’s latest foldable has received the same treatment, with a rather surprising result. YouTuber Zack Nelson, a.k.a. JerryRigEverything , uploaded a durability test video of the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra, starting with the customary scratch test to gauge how the screens will manage under duress. The cover display fares on par with most phones available today, showing faint scratches at level 6 on the Mohs scale, with the scratches becoming more prominent at level 7.

title: I was planning to skip the Pixel 11. These 5 upgrades changed my mind
summary: The Pixel 11 looks familiar, but two years of upgrades add up to a lot.
body: On paper, the Google Pixel 11 doesn’t seem like anything special. It looks like another 2026 smartphone with relatively minor upgrades and a higher starting price, thanks largely to the ongoing RAM and memory crisis. As someone who owns a Pixel 9 from a couple of years ago, upgrading to the Pixel 11 didn’t initially make much sense to me. After all, the Pixel 11 doesn’t look dramatically different from the Pixel 9, and my current phone still works perfectly fine.

title: Samsung isn’t just copying Apple anymore — it is Apple
summary: You can copy Apple’s homework. You can’t copy the reason it works.
body: When the latest leaks and rumors around the Samsung Galaxy S27 Ultra dropped earlier this week, they created a bit of a furor in the Android Authority newsroom, and for good reason. Early renders show a wide horizontal camera bar stretching across the back of the phone. It replaces the individual floating lenses Samsung has used for years for a striking change that also looks suspiciously similar to a certain Pro-themed smartphone from Cupertino. For years, we’ve given Samsung a hard time for playing it safe with iterative designs. Now, I’m not saying that critiquing Samsung’s repetitive takes on the same design ID wasn’t well deserved. However, now that the company is trying out something different, I can’t really say it’s for the better. The problem is not that Samsung changed its design language. It is that the change feels less like a bold step forward and more like Samsung wholeheartedly adopting Apple’s roadmap as its own.

title: Google’s latest attempt at fast wired charging on the Pixel 11 Pro XL is a disaster
summary: What good is Extreme Charging if it doesn't even turn on?
body: If there are two pieces of tech I have a love-hate relationship with, it’s USB-C charging and Google’s Pixel smartphones. At their best, both can be brilliantly hassle-free, but at their worst, they’re a parade of seemingly unnecessary compromises. Based on my previous experiences with Pixels, testing the 45W wired charging capabilities of the new Pixel 11 Pro XL was almost certainly going to cause a headache or two, but it quickly descended into a full-on migraine. Let’s start with the good USB-C news for the Pixel 11 Pro XL. After years of underperforming the headline charging figure, Google’s latest large flagship comes much closer to hitting its 45W marketing claim. While still not quite there, I was able to hit a peak of 40.7W for about the first 9 minutes on the Google Pixel Flex 67W charger (). That’s a reasonable power level and far better sustained than rivals that claim up to 100W capabilities, plus it exceeds the 35W peak I’ve observed on the previous two generations of XL smartphones. So a pat on the back there.

title: Latest Galaxy S26 beta update comes with plenty of goodies from the Fold 8
summary: There's My FanCam, Call Brief, Custom Cards in Now Brief, and more in this new update for the S26.
body: Credit: Paul Jones / Android Authority TL;DR Samsung just released One UI 9 Beta 7 for the Galaxy S26 series, featuring unannounced Galaxy AI additions. Digging in, we’ve found new features: My FanCam video re-framing, Call Brief overlay, Custom Cards in Now Brief, and unified Finder and Google Search home screen search widgets. These features were launched with the Galaxy Z8 foldables and also made available to the Galaxy S26 FE, and are now on track to expand to the Galaxy S26 series when the stable update rolls out. Samsung just rolled out One UI 9 Beta 7 to the Galaxy S26 series with a mysterious “Added new AI features” entry in the changelog. While the company remains tight-lipped, we’ve found that the update introduces several new features, including My FanCam, Call Brief, a Custom Card for Now Brief, and Search and Finder options on the home screen. Starting with the most notable change, you will see the new Google Search and Finder widgets right on your home screen if you previously had the Finder widget there. Samsung now lets you choose one, both, or none, as spotted previously .

title: Samsung doesn’t care about the Galaxy S27, and the leaked renders prove it
summary: I hate the leaked Galaxy S27 design, but Samsung knows exactly what it's doing.
body: Samsung just completed its Galaxy S26 lineup with the launch of the Galaxy S26 FE , and rumors about its next-generation flagships, the Galaxy S27 series, are already circulating. We recently got our first look at the Samsung Galaxy S27 Ultra , which revealed that Samsung could be moving away from its familiar vertical camera layout and instead adopt an iPhone-like horizontal camera plateau. And now, leaks surrounding the base Galaxy S27 have started to surface as well.

title: The first phone with three 200MP cameras (!) is coming soon, and we have high hopes
summary: What could a smartphone do with a 200MP ultrawide camera anyway? Well, plenty in theory.
body: Credit: Robert Triggs / Android Authority TL;DR A trusted leaker has claimed that the OPPO Find X10 Pro Max will be the world’s first phone with three 200MP cameras. This apparently consists of a 200MP HPC main camera, a 200MP telephoto camera, and a 200MP ultrawide shooter. The leaker previously suggested that this phone could launch in September or October. Many smartphones have 200MP sensors, as manufacturers use this for the main or telephoto cameras. However, the OPPO Find X9 Ultra and vivo X300 Ultra stunned us earlier this year by offering two 200MP cameras. It now sounds like a phone with three 200MP cameras is on the horizon. Leaker Digital Chat Station claimed on Weibo that the OPPO Find X10 Pro Max will be the first phone with three 200MP cameras. That means the main, telephoto, and ultrawide cameras will all have 200MP sensors.

title: Gemini Notebook now imports your Google Play Books titles, turning shelfware into notes
summary: Your unfinished ebooks are now Gemini Notebook's problem.
body: Credit: Kaitlyn Cimino / Android Authority TL;DR Google has partnered with authors to make certain paid books available through Gemini Notebook. With the new Expert Intelligence option, users can import certain owned titles from Play Books into Gemini Notebook. Users can also combine insights from multiple titles for a broader knowledge bank in a single notebook. Using copyrighted text for training large language models has been a controversial topic for as long as AI has been a buzzword. That hasn’t stopped frontier labs from gaining access to books, including physical ones, to satisfy the ever-scaling need for pretraining data. The pursuit of high-quality human data has also led to legal troubles for AI companies, including Google, which is now looking to soften the blow by partnering with (and hopefully, rightfully paying) authors — and letting users access and imbibe their wisdom through Gemini Notebook ( previously called NotebookLM ). Gemini Notebook can be an excellent tool for digesting enormous amounts of information in books , but importing books directly may involve wading through gray swamps of skirting DRM restrictions. Google is now formally opening the gates to use …

title: Get ready for YouTubers to start stuffing Amazon affiliate links in their content
summary: YouTube just made it easier for your favorite creators to sell you stuff on Amazon.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR YouTube’s CEO has announced that Amazon is joining the platform’s affiliate program. Eligible creators will now be able to tag Amazon product listings in their videos and earn commission on any purchases made. This could make it easier for you to buy products recommended by the creators you follow. YouTube recently fixed a bug that was hiding saved videos from Watch Later and other playlists. While that’s great, the video platform is in the news again. Not for another bug fix or broken feature, but for a change to the YouTube Shopping affiliate program. In a social media post , YouTube CEO Neal Mohan announced that Amazon is joining its e-commerce network. As a result of this partnership, eligible US YouTube creators will now be able to tag Amazon products in their content. This includes long-form videos, livestreams, and Shorts.

title: Lost Google Maps’ big navigation upgrade? Your new Pixel 11 might be to blame
summary: Immersive Navigation is missing for some.
body: TL;DR Some Pixel 11 owners are losing Google Maps’ Immersive Navigation after upgrading from older phones. The feature seems to be controlled on the server-side, so users can’t simply restore it with an app update or setting. Google is investigating the reports, but it hasn’t confirmed what’s causing the problem or when it’ll be fixed. Buying a new phone shouldn’t feel like a downgrade. For those upgrading from an older Pixel to a new Pixel 11 series device , that’s apparently exactly what’s happening, at least when it comes to their Google Maps experience. Users with the new Pixel 11 are reporting having no access to Immersive Navigation in Google Maps, even if they had it on an earlier device. For many, the “biggest navigation upgrade,” as described by Google, was previously available on their older Android phones. The problem seems to be affecting Immersive Navigation on phones and when running Google Maps through Android Auto , as users report on Reddit and Google’s support forums (via Auto Evolution ).

title: Meta fixes distressingly obvious smart glasses recording LED loophole
summary: You won't believe how easy it was to bypass Meta privacy protections.
body: TL;DR Meta’s smart glasses attempt to detect when their recording LED is blocked or tampered with, and will refuse to start filming. It turns out this check was only performed when recordings were initiated, and users could just start filming and cover the LED afterwards. Meta is currently rolling out a fix to correct this behavior. Retro gamers may remember the old PlayStation 1 swap trick: The system would only check disc integrity when first booting, so you could run imports or backups by first powering the PlayStation up with a legit disc in it, and then quickly swapping it out. It turns out that Meta’s smart glasses have been vulnerable to a similar attack, and the company is only just now getting around to patching it. Everybody’s concerned about smart glasses and privacy right now, and probably the biggest issue there is centered on surreptitious recording. Even though we all carry around phones capable of sneakily recording videos, some folks are just really upset about the idea that someone could film them with smart glasses, and they’d never know it. Responding to that pressure, manufacturers like Meta have been building their glasses with conspicuous recording LEDs, bro…

title: Google Messages has another chat problem users didn’t ask for
summary: Some conversations are suddenly turning into multiple threads.
body: TL;DR Google is investigating a bug that splits existing group chats into separate threads with the same participants. Affected users can end up with multiple versions of the same conversation, sometimes losing the continuity of their chat history. Similar reports involve individual RCS chats, but Google has yet to confirm whether they are related to the acknowledged group-chat bug. Google Messages users haven’t exactly had a quiet summer. Google recently acknowledged an RCS connection bug affecting some users, and the company is still working with its carrier partners to get that problem under control. Now, another Messages problem has surfaced, and this one can leave your conversations scattered across multiple threads. Google has confirmed that it is investigating an issue where group chats split into separate threads. Responding to an affected user on Reddit, Google said its team is actively looking into the problem and asked users to submit feedback through the Messages app with the hashtag #splittingthreads to help engineers investigate.

title: Visible is bundling your phone and fiber, because two bills are one too many
summary: Mobile plan and fiber together for $55/month.
body: TL;DR Visible One bundles mobile and fiber internet on a single bill, starting at $55/month for 300Mbps fiber and Visible’s standard mobile plan. Visible+ Pro One costs $75/month and upgrades you to 1Gbps fiber plus Visible’s premium mobile plan with 5G Ultra Wideband and a smartwatch line. There are no added taxes, fees, contracts, or credit checks, but the bundles are limited to homes that already have an inactive Fios ONT installed. Soon after debuting its 5G home internet option, Verizon MVNO Visible is now introducing a new bundle that combines its mobile services and fiber home internet. Aptly named Visible One , the new bundle is offered through Visible Fiber, with the company leaning heavily into its no-hidden-fees, no-annual-contracts, and no-credit-check approach to attract price-conscious consumers.

title: Homey just solved one of the biggest smart home problems
summary: You can now update Matter, Zigbee, and Z-Wave devices directly from the Homey app.
body: TL;DR Homey now lets users install over-the-air (OTA) firmware updates for connected smart home devices directly from a single app. Matter, Zigbee, and Z-Wave devices are supported, covering thousands of products from multiple manufacturers. The new feature, known as Device Updates, will be available with the Homey app version 9.10.0 and newer, as well as the Homey web experience. Not all smart home setups look alike. Mixing and matching devices from multiple brands is common, as it gives you the flexibility to choose something within your budget. However, managing products from a variety of manufacturers can be a tad irritating, especially when it’s time for a firmware update. Smart home platform Homey has now addressed this particular pain point by enabling over-the-air (OTA) updates for multiple major smart home protocols from its app. In a blog post announcing the changes, Homey shares that owners of Matter, Zigbee, and Z-Wave devices can now download updates directly from the Homey app. Updates for Zigbee and Z-Wave devices will come from their respective apps within Homey, while Matter device owners will receive updates through the Connectivity Standards Alliance’s Distribut…

title: Google Messages now lets you give every chat its own look
summary: Custom chat themes and wallpapers let you give each conversation the vibe it deserves.
body: TL;DR Google Messages is rolling out custom chat themes and wallpapers after months of testing. You can use preset backgrounds or your own photos, with matching message bubble colors. Themes are private to you, and RCS must be enabled to use them. We first spotted Google working on custom chat themes for Messages back in May — a feature that users of some other messaging apps have had for a while. Google is finally catching up on that front today, announcing that users can personalize individual conversations with custom colors and wallpapers. In a Messages Community post , Google explained that users can now change both message bubble colors and chat backgrounds. You can choose one of Google’s preset wallpapers, pick an image from your own gallery, or stick with a simpler color theme.

title: Pixel 11 users report bursts of static noise ruining their videos
summary: An audio glitch is ruining videos recorded on Pixel 11 phones.
body: Credit: Dhruv Bhutani / Android Authority TL;DR Pixel 11 series users are reporting an issue with Video Boost. Bursts of static noise appear at intervals in videos recorded with the feature enabled. The issue may have something to do with an Audio Zoom bug. As we move further away from the launch of the Pixel 11 series , Google’s latest and greatest handsets are getting into more hands. That means a growing number of people are now putting the smartphones through their paces to see what they can do. Some users who were testing out the video recording capabilities have discovered a strange and frustrating issue with zoomed-in video. One Redditor who upgraded to the Pixel 11 Pro XL says they attended a house show the other night to test out the camera. When they reviewed their recordings, they noticed “static bursts” every five seconds. According to the poster, this issue only appeared on videos where Video Boost was enabled.

title: Thinking of trading in a Pixel 10 for the new Pixel 11? Read this first
summary: Pixel 10 trade-ins for the Pixel 11 sound completely broken.
body: TL;DR Pixel 11 shoppers report serious problems when trying to get a Pixel 10 trade-in credit with Google. They describe conflicting messages about trade-in acceptance and unexpected card charges. One theory suggests this stems from a problem with a partner company processing trade-ins. For smartphone fans who always need to have the latest and greatest handset, trade-in deals can be a great way to upgrade every year without needing to pay full price every time. And while that normally works fine, when you’ve got hundreds of dollars on the line, all it takes is one small glitch in the process for you to have a very bad day. Sadly, that’s exactly what a number of Pixel users seem to be dealing with right now, as they report some confusing issues that are interfering with trade-ins. Over on Reddit’s Pixel sub, Pixel 10 owners are sharing their frustrations with trying to trade last year’s phone in for a new Pixel 11 on the Google Store.

title: The AOC wireless headset with mic mute and 45-hour battery falls to just $45.99
summary: This AOC wireless work headset is 23% off at Amazon, with clear call focus, Bluetooth, a USB dongle, and 4.8-star reviews.
body: The AOC Wireless Headset with Microphone for Work is built for people who spend a lot of time on calls, video meetings, and remote work, and it’s on sale right now at Amazon. It focuses on clear voice pickup and flexible wireless use, which makes it a strong fit for office desks, home setups, and work on the go. See the deal at Amazon

title: Record deal: Philips Hue Neon Outdoor lightstrip hits its best price yet at 28% off
summary: Amazon cuts $56 off the Philips Hue Neon Outdoor 16-foot lightstrip, a smart neon-style outdoor light for patios and fences.
body: Outdoor spaces can look flat once the sun goes down, especially around patios, walkways, fences, and garden edges. The Philips Hue Neon Outdoor 16-Feet Multicolor LED Strip Light is built for exactly that kind of job, and there’s a record Amazon deal on it right now. See the deal at Amazon

title: Samsung’s Galaxy S27 Pro finally breaks cover, and it looks familiar
summary: The S27 Ultra's reported iPhone-like design could make its way to the S27 Pro.
body: TL;DR Samsung’s Galaxy S27 Pro has surfaced in detailed renders for the first time, revealing an iPhone 17 Pro-inspired camera design. The Pro is expected to share much of the S27 Ultra’s hardware, but with a smaller 6.6-inch display and no built-in S Pen. A 5,200mAh battery could make the S27 Pro a smaller, easier-to-handle alternative to Samsung’s giant Ultra. The release of Samsung’s Galaxy S27 series reveal is roughly five months away at this point, but that’s not stopping early leaks and rumors from shedding light on what the upcoming devices might look like. The latest in the series of leaks gives us our first clear look at the Galaxy S27 Pro. We got our first-ever look at renders of the S27 Ultra earlier this week, which were followed by the base Galaxy S27 breaking cover. And now, thanks to the folks over at Android Headlines , we have finally have clear S27 Pro renders.

title: Android 17 has some new tricks to keep your web traffic private
summary: Here's how Android 17 is locking down your network traffic from prying eyes.
body: TL;DR Google’s implementing a number of new network security upgrades for Android 17. Encrypted Client Hello attempts to solve DNS privacy problems by encrypting server lookups. SMS Blaster protection empowers carriers to block low-security 2G connections by default. Keeping mobile devices secure is one of those jobs that never end, and when it comes to security in Android, Google finds itself constantly working to lock our phones down against external threats. With Android 17 , the company’s already highlighted some of the big ways it’s been improving security , and today Google has a few more updates to share on how your phone is becoming more secure and private that ever. Android 17 makes a number of changes to how devices work with network traffic. One big privacy-protecting one there impacts how apps are able to see your home’s local network, preventing them from probing it for fingerprinting or even spotting vulnerable network hardware. Another we knew about implements Certificate Transparency by default, helping ensure that your phone uses the proper SSL certificates for the server it’s trying to communicate with.

title: YouTube just brought back the videos users thought they had lost
summary: Your saved videos in Watch Later and other playlists should now be showing up where they belong.
body: TL;DR YouTube has confirmed it fixed the bug that was hiding videos from Watch Later and other playlists. Affected users reported missing videos, ‘playlist does not exist’ errors, and broken playlists across mobile and desktop. YouTube hasn’t said what caused the issue or whether an app update is needed, but affected users should now see their full playlists again. Watch Later is one of those YouTube features you don’t appreciate until it stops working. It is the easiest way to stash a video you don’t have time for, build a queue for later, or simply keep track of something you don’t want to lose. So, having videos mysteriously disappear from the playlist over the past few weeks has understandably been frustrating for some users. The good news is that YouTube says the problem is now fixed. YouTube confirmed the fix in a forum post earlier today, telling affected users that all their videos should now display correctly in their playlists, including Watch Later on the YouTube app.

title: The Galaxy Watch is experiencing an odd restart bug after a recent update, here’s how to fix it
summary: Make sure your Galaxy Watch charger is nearby.
body: TL;DR Some Galaxy Watch owners are facing a bug where the smartwatch refuses to boot after being prompted to restart. The restart is triggered as part of a harmless time zone update, but the watch seemingly refuses to turn on after that. Thankfully, the smartwatch can reportedly be brought back to life by placing it on the charging puck. Samsung’s Galaxy Watch variants consistently rank among the best smartwatches in the business. However, like with any hardware, bugs and glitches can pop up from time to time, and we can now report on one such case involving Samsung’s premium smartwatch model. According to SamMobile , a Galaxy Watch Ultra at their disposal was prompted to restart after a time zone update. It’s not uncommon for this message to appear, particularly if you’ve switched time zones recently. However, the site found that the smartwatch refused to boot after pressing restart.

title: Which smartphone has the best battery life? I tested dozens to find the winner
summary: Always wanted multi-day battery life? These are the phones you should buy.
body: If there’s one thing we all want from our next smartphone , it’s more battery life. Thankfully, battery cells are bigger than ever, while processors are increasingly frugal. This means that many, but certainly not all, flagship and mid-range handsets can take us through a day without leaving us suffering from battery anxiety. However, some phones are definitely better than others at lasting through more demanding work/life balances or taking lighter users through a second day. Not to mention, there’s a massive variation in how quickly phones charge back up when they eventually run out of power.

title: 5 Bluetooth trackers you should buy instead of the Google Pixel Tag
summary: Keep track of all your important items, no matter where you are.
body: Google finally built its own Bluetooth tracker called the Pixel Tag , priced at $29. It has nearly everything we hoped for from Google’s debut tracker, including a minimalist/waterproof design, a replaceable battery, Ultra-Wideband (UWB) support for precision tracking, a built-in speaker, and unique ecosystem integration with non-smartphone Pixel devices. There’s just one problem: you’ll have to wait until November to buy one. Thankfully, there are plenty of solid alternatives to the Pixel Tag already on sale today. Most of them already work with Google’s Find Hub network and offer features similar to the Pixel Tag. In fact, a few of them even support USB-C or wireless charging, and can be as slim as a credit card.
